title: Wait times at two urgent care clinics

stimulus.title: Wait times at two urgent care clinics
stimulus.text: A health network recorded the wait time, in minutes, of 20 randomly selected patients at each of its two urgent care clinics, North and South, during one month (invented data). The boxplots and summary statistics are below.

plot.label: Parallel boxplots of wait times in minutes for 20 patients at each clinic. North: box from 19.5 to 30, median 24.5, whiskers from 12 to 41. South: box from 13.5 to 31, median 18.5, whiskers from 8 to 52, one outlier at 70.

parts.label: a
parts.prompt: Compare the distributions of wait times at the two clinics. Address shape, center, variability and unusual features, in context.

rubric.point: Shape compared: North roughly symmetric, South skewed right (toward longer waits)
accept: North is roughly symmetric and South is skewed right
South has a long right tail and North does not

rubric.point: Center compared with a comparing word and values: South has a lower median wait (18.5 minutes) than North (24.5 minutes)
accept: the median wait at North is greater than at South (24.5 vs 18.5)
means may be compared too (25.2 vs 24.5) if the response says which is greater

rubric.point: Variability compared with values: South is more variable (IQR 17.5 vs 10.5 minutes, or SD 16.0 vs 7.8, or range 62 vs 29)
accept: South’s wait times are more spread out than North’s, with a measure named
naming IQR, SD or range with values for both clinics

rubric.point: Unusual features: South has a high outlier at 70 minutes; North has no outliers
accept: one South patient waited 70 minutes, an outlier
no outliers at North and one at South

parts.sample: The distribution of wait times at North is roughly symmetric, while the distribution at South is skewed right. South has a lower median wait (18.5 minutes) than North (24.5 minutes). South’s wait times are much more variable, with an IQR of 17.5 minutes compared with 10.5 minutes at North. South has one high outlier, a patient who waited 70 minutes; North has no outliers.

parts.label: b
parts.prompt: Use the 1.5 × IQR rule to determine whether the 70-minute wait at South is an outlier. Show your work.

rubric.point: Correct upper fence for South with work: Q3 + 1.5(IQR) = 31 + 1.5(17.5) = 57.25 minutes
Correct conclusion in context: 70 > 57.25, so the 70-minute wait is an outlier
accept: because 70 is above the upper fence, it is an outlier

parts.sample: IQR = Q3 - Q1 = 31 - 13.5 = 17.5. Upper fence = Q3 + 1.5(IQR) = 31 + 1.5(17.5) = 57.25 minutes. Because 70 > 57.25, the 70-minute wait at South is an outlier.

parts.label: c
parts.prompt: One patient waited 35 minutes at North and another waited 40 minutes at South. Calculate the z-score of each wait using the summary statistics, and identify which wait was more unusual for its clinic.

rubric.point: Both z-scores with work: North z = (35 - 25.2)/7.8 = 1.26; South z = (40 - 24.5)/16.0 = 0.97
accept: z = (value - mean)/SD for each, values within rounding

rubric.point: Correct comparison: the 35-minute wait at North is more unusual, because it is more standard deviations above its clinic’s mean (1.26 vs 0.97)
accept: North’s wait, since its z-score is larger
a comparison that uses the z-scores, not the raw waits

parts.sample: North: z = (35 - 25.2)/7.8 = 1.26. South: z = (40 - 24.5)/16.0 = 0.97. The 35-minute wait at North is more unusual for its clinic, because it is 1.26 standard deviations above North’s mean wait, while the 40-minute wait is only 0.97 standard deviations above South’s mean wait.

parts.label: d
parts.prompt: A patient wants the better chance of being seen within 20 minutes. Which clinic should the patient choose? Justify your answer using the boxplots or summary statistics.

rubric.point: Justification from a statistic: South’s median, 18.5, is under 20, so more than half of South’s patients waited under 20 minutes; North’s median, 24.5, is over 20, so fewer than half did (North’s Q1, 19.5, is near 20, so only about a quarter did)
accept: compares the position of 20 relative to the two medians or quartiles
a justification that uses the center or quartiles, not the outlier or the means alone

parts.sample: South. The median wait at South is 18.5 minutes, which is less than 20, so more than half of the South patients waited less than 20 minutes. At North the median is 24.5 minutes, and Q1 is 19.5, so only about a quarter of North patients waited 20 minutes or less.
